questions.question: What can a person export in the first version?
questions.context: Every one of the 212 tickets asks about sending a single note. A whole notebook as one PDF needs page breaks between notes and a table of contents. I recommend one note at a time, because that is what people ask for.

options.label: One note at a time
options.consequence: Export as PDF sits in each note's menu.
options.tradeoff: Someone who wants a whole notebook exports it note by note.

options.label: A note or a whole notebook
options.consequence: A notebook becomes one PDF, with each note starting on a new page.
options.tradeoff: About a week more, and a large notebook makes a large file.

answer.note: The tickets ask about one note, so notebooks can wait for a second version.

questions.question: What happens to content a PDF cannot hold, such as a video or a link to another note?
questions.context: A note can embed videos, audio clips and links to other notes. None of these work on paper, and a link to another note opens nothing outside the app. I recommend a short line of text in place of each, so the reader knows something was there.

options.label: A short line of text in its place
options.consequence: A video shows as "Video: Kitchen tour, 2 minutes".
options.tradeoff: One renderer case per kind of embed, about a day of work.

options.label: Leave it out
options.consequence: The PDF holds only text and images.
options.tradeoff: No extra work, but the reader cannot tell that anything is missing.

answer.note: A reader should see that something was there, even when it cannot play.

questions.question: Where does Export as PDF sit?
questions.context: The note menu holds Copy link and Duplicate today. The share sheet is where people send things on a phone. I recommend the note menu, because it is where Copy as markdown already lives.

options.label: In the note menu
options.consequence: Export as PDF sits beside Copy as markdown.
options.tradeoff: People who look in the share sheet first will not find it there.

options.label: In the note menu and the share sheet
options.consequence: Both places show Export as PDF.
options.tradeoff: Two entry points to keep the same, and the share sheet differs on each phone.

answer.note: One place is easier to explain in the help pages.

questions.question: What happens when an export fails halfway, for example when the disk is full?
questions.context: `export/pdf.ts` writes the file page by page, so a failure leaves part of a PDF behind. A partial PDF opens without an error and looks finished. I recommend deleting it and saying what went wrong.

options.label: Delete the partial file and show a plain error
options.consequence: The person sees "Your disk is full. Free some space and export again."
options.tradeoff: The work done so far is lost, which costs seconds for a normal note.

options.label: Keep the partial file and mark it incomplete
options.consequence: The file name ends in "incomplete" and the person sees a warning.
options.tradeoff: A partial file can still be sent by mistake.

answer.note: Half a PDF looks finished to whoever receives it.

questions.question: Who do people send these PDFs to?
questions.context: In the last round of eight interviews, five people mentioned sending notes to a teacher, a client or a landlord. Two wanted to print notes for themselves. I recommend designing for people outside the app, because that is the larger group.

options.label: People outside the app
options.consequence: The PDF carries the note's title and date at the top, so it makes sense on its own.
options.tradeoff: A header the person may not want when they print for themselves.

options.label: The person, to print
options.consequence: The PDF holds only the note's content, sized for paper.
options.tradeoff: Someone who receives it has no title or date to go by.

answer.note: Five of the eight people we spoke to send notes to someone else.

questions.question: Does the PDF need tags so a screen reader can follow it?
questions.context: A PDF without tags reads as one block of text, with no headings and no list items. The renderer already knows the structure, so tagging costs little. I recommend a tagged PDF.

options.label: A tagged PDF with headings, lists and reading order
options.consequence: A screen reader announces each heading and list item.
options.tradeoff: About two days more, and a file a few percent larger.

options.label: A plain PDF
options.consequence: The PDF looks the same but reads as one block.
options.tradeoff: Ships sooner, and leaves out people who use a screen reader.

answer.note: Teachers we spoke to have to accept files a screen reader can read.

questions.question: Which number tells us the export works for people?
questions.context: Support gets about 70 tickets a month that ask for PDF or print. Exports per week shows use but not success. I recommend the ticket count, because it is the problem this plan sets out to fix.

options.label: Fewer PDF tickets to support
options.consequence: The goal is under 10 a month, two months after release.
options.tradeoff: Slow to read, since tickets lag behind a release by weeks.

options.label: Exports per week for each active person
options.consequence: A chart on the release dashboard from the first day.
options.tradeoff: It shows people use it, not that the PDF was right.

answer.note: The tickets are why we are building this, so they are the number to move.

questions.question: Can a person export a note someone else shared with them?
questions.context: A shared note can be read but not changed by the people it is shared with. Copy as markdown already works on shared notes, so a person can copy the text today. I recommend allowing export, because it gives away nothing a copy does not.

options.label: Yes, the same as Copy as markdown
options.consequence: Export as PDF shows on every note the person can read.
options.tradeoff: An owner cannot stop a reader from making a file.

options.label: Only notes the person owns
options.consequence: Export as PDF is greyed out on shared notes, with a line that says why.
options.tradeoff: Readers copy the text instead, so it protects little.

answer.note: Blocking it protects nothing while Copy as markdown works.

questions.question: What do we tell someone whose PDF looks different from the note?
questions.context: A PDF drops videos, uses the light theme and splits tall images. People will write in when the file does not match the screen. I recommend a help page linked from the export dialog, because one page answers every case.

options.label: A help page linked from the export dialog
options.consequence: The dialog shows "What changes in a PDF" with a link.
options.tradeoff: People who skip the dialog still write in.

options.label: A saved reply for the support team
options.consequence: Support answers each ticket with the same text.
options.tradeoff: Every person who is confused still has to write in first.

answer.note: A page people find on their own saves them a ticket and a wait.
